marks.gloss_en: ותניא, רבי דוסתאי בר מתון אומר: מותר להתגרות ברשעים בעולם הזה -- the baraita restates the permission (his commit at 6b.6); kind svara: no SupportKind names ותניא
ואם לחשך אדם לומר: אל תתחר במרעים ואל תקנא בעושי עולה
מי שלבו נוקפו אומר כן
איני? והאמר רבי יוחנן משום רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: מותר להתגרות ברשעים בעולם הזה (kind svara under protest: no ObjectionKind names an amoraic-memra contradiction)
it is permitted to provoke the wicked in this world
דאמר רב הונא: ...צדיק ממנו בולע, צדיק גמור אינו בולע
ואיבעית אימא: הא והא במילי דידיה -- הא בצדיק גמור, הא בצדיק שאינו גמור (= p_okimta_tzadik_gamur)
answer 2: both concern his own affairs -- this of a completely righteous man, that of one not completely righteous
אלא: אל תתחר במרעים -- להיות כמרעים (= p_al_titchar_lihyot)
R' Dostai: rather, 'do not contend with evildoers' -- to be like evildoers; 'do not envy the workers of iniquity' -- to be like the workers of iniquity
לא קשיא: הא במילי דידיה, הא במילי דשמיא (= p_okimta_milei_dishmaya)
answer 1: no difficulty -- this [the warning] concerns his own affairs, that [the permission] matters of Heaven
ואי בעית אימא: שעה משחקת לו שאני (= p_okimta_shaah_mesachekat)
answer 3: when the hour smiles on him it is different
'do not further his device' -- this is Germamya of Edom, who, were they to go forth, would destroy the whole world

R' Chama bar Chanina: there are three hundred crowned princes in Germamya of Edom and three hundred sixty-five chieftains in Rome; each day these go out against those, one of them is killed, and they are busied appointing a king
R' Yitzchak: if a man says 'I toiled and did not find', do not believe; 'I did not toil and found', do not believe; 'I toiled and found', believe
the stam: that holds in words of Torah; in trade it is help from Heaven
R' Yitzchak: if you see a wicked man on whom the hour smiles, do not provoke him
if they read the Megilla in the first Adar and the year was intercalated, they read it in the second Adar
Italya of Yavan is the great city of Rome
one who dwells in it, though not born in it, receives an allowance from the king's house
הא לענין סדר פרשיות זה וזה שוין -- from אין בין ... אלא
the stam: it follows that for the order of the portions, this [Adar] and that are equal
אי תנא קמא — קשיא מתנות: TK excepts only the Megilla, but the mishna counts gifts to the poor as a difference
אי רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי — קשיא נמי מקרא מגילה: for him not even the Megilla is a difference
אי רבן שמעון בן גמליאל — קשיא סדר פרשיות: for him the portions too differ, yet the mishna implies they are equal (6b.14)
the mishna is REBY's
if they read the Megilla in the first Adar and the year was intercalated, they read it in the second Adar (TK; RSBG: אף קורין אותה באדר השני)
REBY: they do not read it in the second Adar
RSBG: the mitzvot practised in the second are not practised in the first
Rav Pappa: the order of the portions is [the difference] between them (TK and RSBG)
REBY (per Rav Pappa): even the reading of the Megilla ab initio in the first
the mishna is TK's
the mishna is RSBG's
the halakha follows RSBG, who said it in R' Yosei's name
REBY expounds 'in each and every year' (Esther 9:21): as every year it is the Adar next to Shevat, so here the Adar next to Shevat
RSBG expounds 'in each and every year': as every year it is the Adar next to Nisan, so here the Adar next to Nisan
REBY's reason is reasonable: one does not pass over mitzvot
R' Tavi: RSBG's reason is that joining redemption to redemption is preferable
R' Elazar: RSBG's reason is from 'to confirm this second letter of Purim' (Esther 9:29)
